articles.title: 2 die, several feared trapped in Delhi's Chawri Bazar building collapse; MCD says owner continued work in guise of repairs
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A four-storey under-construction building collapsed in central Delhi's Chawri Bazar Thursday, killing two labourers and injuring many others.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A four-storey under-construction building collapsed in central Delhi's Chawri Bazar Thursday, killing two labourers and injuring many others. Several people are still feared trapped in the rubble.Locals said around 15 people were working at the site when the building collapsed around 9.30am.The structure’s third floor gave way as workers were laying the lintel, bringing down the building, officials and residents said.Delhi Fire Service officials said seven people had been pulled out of the rubble with two succumbing to injuries. Teams from Delhi Police, NDRF, Delhi Fire Service and MCD are still looking for others who might be trapped. This is the fourth major building collapse in three months in Delhi.The deceased have been identified as Kishori, 40, and Sanjeet, 45, and among the injured were Sahdev Chaudhary, 25, and Firoz, 37.All four lived in Mandawali’s Railway Colony. An FIR under Section 105 BNS (culpable homicide not amounting to murder) against building owner Samiullah and contractors has been registered.A senior police officer said they had alerted MCD about the unauthorised construction nearly five months ago.MCD said it conducted an inspection, during which the owner was found undertaking repair work. It said no subsequent complaint about fresh construction or demolition of the building was received later.MCD suspended an assistant and a junior engineer for prima facie “severe dereliction of duty” pending further inquiry. CM Rekha Gupta along with minister Ashish Sood and Union MoS Harsh Malhotra inspected the spot.Police sources said the building was not constructed properly and quality of construction material may have been poor. “They were adding more floors, but the foundation may not have been strong enough," sources said.‘Heard Two Loud Bangs, Homes Started Shaking’“The two loud bangs were followed by the neighbouring buildings shaking. We rushed to the spot and started clearing the rubble. We rescued as many injured people as we could,” said Khaleel, who had just walked past the lane when the building collapsed.Recalling the incident, Naeem, a neighbour, said, “I was having breakfast when I heard a loud noise. I rushed downstairs and saw a labourer running from the collapse site. He had injuries on his back, shoulder and hands.”Another resident, Md Huzaif, said one labourer managed to save himself by holding on to a pillar as the structure came down. “Neighbours tied ropes and pulled him up to an adjacent house,” he said.The building stood opposite a mosque, prompting concerns among residents about what could have happened had it collapsed during prayers.“We are lucky it did not collapse during namaz. Otherwise, many more people might have been trapped. It was probably for the first time that the mosque had been shut; even during the pandemic one or two people would come for prayers,” Huzaif said.Locals alleged the building was being constructed in haste ahead of the winter curbs on construction.Kamran Hashmi, a resident, claimed three floors had come up in just over a month. According to him, the building and an adjoining structure belonged to the same family. The old structure, which had two floors, was demolished a few months ago to make way for a five-storey building, he alleged.“They gave only two days for the lintel to strengthen before beginning construction work on the next floor,” a neighbour claimed.The site was divided between two brothers, locals said. While one’s five-storey structure had been completed, the other’s was under construction.Meanwhile, the collapse left families of workers waiting anxiously for word of their loved ones.Birender, whose brother Pankaj, a native of Bihar’s Khagaria, was working at the site, said he had been unable to contact him since morning.“I received the news from a relative. When I called him, his phone was switched off. There is no news of him so far. He had been working at the construction site for the past six months. articles.title: ‘Bolt from the blue’: Israeli president shocked as Trump moves to end annual US aid
articles.summary: Israeli president Isaac Herzog has said US President Donald Trump's announcement that Washington would end its annual military aid to Israel came as a
articles.body: Israeli president Isaac Herzog has said US President Donald Trump's announcement that Washington would end its annual military aid to Israel came as a surprise, describing it as “like a bolt from the blue”, amid growing political debate in the United States over military assistance to its Middle East ally.Herzog raised the issue during a meeting with the Yashar party, led by Gadi Eisenkot, a key rival of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. He expressed concern over the decision, pointing out that the existing US-Israel memorandum of understanding (MoU) on military assistance was due to remain in force until 2028.“The issue of the American aid worries me greatly, and it also fell on me like a bolt from the blue. We have an (memorandum of understanding) with the US that is supposed to last until 2028 and this is one of the major goals, and therefore a government must be formed and not go to repeated elections,” Herzog said.Trump announced on Tuesday, as Americans voted in the midterm elections, that he had reached an agreement with Netanyahu to end the $4 billion in annual US funding to Israel after this year. However, he said Washington would continue selling weapons to its close Middle East ally.The announcement marked a significant shift in US policy, particularly as the existing agreement provides Israel with $3.8 billion in annual military assistance until September 2028. Trump did not explain how the funding would be halted before the agreement expires.The US president appeared to acknowledge that military aid to Israel had become a political liability for Republicans, saying the move was partly intended to remove a "bad talking point" that left-wing Democrats had used against his party over its support for Israel.The announcement also drew attention to growing divisions within the Republican Party over the relationship with Israel. Vice President JD Vance had said on X that the US-Israel relationship contributed to Republican losses in the midterm elections.US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee said he was seeking clarification on how the proposed change would be implemented. In an interview with Israel's Channel 12 News, he defended continued military assistance and disputed the suggestion that support for Israel had become politically damaging among Republicans.“Americans need to know the value of the relationship,” he said. “It’s not about what Americans are putting into it. It’s about what they are getting out of it. Maybe we haven’t done a good job helping the American public to recognize and be grateful for the partnership with Israel, which has benefited their lives every day.”Disagreeing with Vance's assessment, Huckabee added, “I don’t think support for Israel is toxic in the conservative wing and the Republican Party.”US military assistance to Israel has faced growing opposition across both Democratic and Republican circles, weakening what had long been a bipartisan consensus in Washington. Analysts suggested that Trump's announcement on Election Day was partly aimed at addressing criticism of US support for Israel among voters.Discussions had already been underway on the future of American assistance beyond 2028, with Netanyahu previously indicating that he expected US aid to gradually wind down. Trump, however, appeared to signal that he had decided to accelerate the process.The announcement comes as the United States and Israel remain engaged in a conflict with Iran, more than eight months after jointly launching attacks against the Islamic Republic.You use AI every day. articles.title: Russia and Ukraine exchange airstrikes as U.S. envoy describes renewed security talks as productive
articles.summary: The latest Russian barrage underscored the scale of the rebuilding task, as did the ongoing search for people missing after an earlier strike.
articles.body: KYIV, Ukraine — Russia and Ukraine exchanged airstrikes overnight as the second day of talks on Ukraine’s postwar reconstruction and security guarantees once the fighting ends wrapped up in Brussels on Thursday. The latest Russian aerial barrage underscored the scale of the rebuilding task, as did the continuing search for people missing beneath the rubble after a deadly airstrike in southern Ukraine on Monday. Ukraine launched hundreds of drones at Russian targets. Russia’s Defense Ministry said its forces shot down nearly 500 drones overnight. A Ukrainian attack on a bus killed five people and wounded 13 others Thursday in Ukraine’s Russian-occupied Luhansk region, according to Leonid Pasechnik, the region’s Moscow-backed leader. Further details were not immediately available. Meanwhile, rescue teams continued searching for more than 30 people believed trapped in the wreckage of a former school and a nearby shelter hit by Russian guided bombs on Monday. The attack in Komyshuvakha, near the front line in the Zaporizhzhia region, struck as residents waited for humanitarian aid. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said 43 people had been confirmed dead. In a message on X, he said one person previously reported missing had been found alive. Postwar reconstruction talks resume The second day of talks wrapped up at NATO headquarters in Brussels as officials from the U.S., the U.K., France, Germany and the European Union discussed postwar reconstruction, funding for 2027 and security guarantees backed by the Ukrainian government’s Western allies. Ukraine’s lead negotiator Rustem Umerov said that representatives from the World Bank and the U.S. investment group BlackRock were also present. “We separately discussed the threats from Russia to Ukraine and all of Europe, as well as joint steps to counter them,” Umerov wrote in an online post. Jared Kushner, U.S. President Donald Trump’s son-in-law and peace envoy, described the meeting as “productive and substantive.” The Brussels meetings are taking place days before negotiators from Russia, Ukraine and the United States are due to meet in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, for talks aimed at trying to end the war. Late Wednesday, Zelenskyy said that he had held a 90-minute conversation with U.S. negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. “The negotiations must move forward at full throttle to bring this war to an end as quickly as possible,” Zelenskyy said on X. “Ukraine is ready to take the necessary steps. Our proposals are clear, and we have given them to the American side.” In excerpts from an interview with German broadcaster ZDF, to be aired in full on Friday, Zelenskyy expressed hope that the Democratic Party’s win in the U.S. midterm elections could usher in a new era of support for Ukraine. “We have support from two parties — support from both parties. I am also grateful to the Republicans,” Zelenskyy said. He added that the Democrats “speak of renewing the ties between the U.S. and Europe, which have been somewhat lost in recent years. And that is very important to us.” Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna told The Associated Press that the midterm results could change the atmosphere in Washington. “The understanding that Russia is an aggressive country and is not serving U.S. interests” may become more prevalent on Capitol Hill after the elections, Tsahkna said in Tallinn, Estonia’s capital. But “the president is President Trump,” he added, and Trump can dictate foreign and security policy. Ukraine’s situation will depend in part on Trump’s actions, Tsahkna said, and the president may feel freer to act because he is not running for re-election. “Unpredictability” should be expected, he said. Ukraine receives further $4.9 billion from Europe The European Commission on Thursday sent Ukraine 4.4 billion euros ($4.9 billion) as part of a 90 billion-euro ($100 billion) loan agreed in April by E.U. leaders to support the embattled nation. Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said that the money will help Ukraine fund essential spending on defense and public services. “As Russia continues its relentless attacks, Ukraine is about to start its fifth wartime winter,” she said. “And as efforts to achieve a just and lasting peace for Ukraine continue, so too does the E.U.’s unwavering support.” Russian airstrikes wound 4 in Ukraine Ukraine’s air defenses shot down or suppressed 105 of 128 Russian attack drones overnight and into early Thursday, while Russian strikes wounded four people in the eastern Dnipropetrovsk and Kyiv regions, Ukrainian officials said. Russian drones struck six areas in the Dnipropetrovsk region, wounding three people in the city of Dnipro, regional administrator Oleksandr Hanzha said. A Russian attack on logistics infrastructure west of the capital, Kyiv, caused a fire and wounded a man, the State Emergency Service said. Fire reported at Russian oil refinery Russia’s Defense Ministry said Thursday that its forces shot down 496 Ukrainian drones over 13 Russian regions overnight, as well as the Crimean Peninsula, which was annexed by Russia, and the Black and Azov seas. More than 200 Ukrainian drones targeted Russia’s Ryazan region southeast of Moscow, wounding one person, local governor Pavel Malkov said. Malkov said that falling debris from the attack damaged power lines and sparked a fire at an industrial site. Russian media outlets later reported a blaze at the Ryazan oil refinery, sharing pictures of plumes of smoke and the night sky glowing red.

articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Friday said the results of the US midterm elections would have little impact on India-US relations, asserting
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Friday said the results of the US midterm elections would have little impact on India-US relations, asserting that President Donald Trump retains considerable powers to pursue his foreign policy agenda despite the ruling party's electoral setback.Speaking in Thiruvananthapuram, Tharoor said the US election results would not change Washington's approach towards key issues such as tariffs, sanctions on countries buying Russian oil, the Iran war or the Ukraine conflict."Whether it comes to tariffs, whether it comes to sanctions for buying Russian oil, whether it comes to the Iran war itself, whether it comes to any initiative he takes on the Ukraine war. All of this, he's completely unaffected by the election result," Tharoor said.He explained that while Congress has significant powers over budgetary matters and can restrict or approve government spending, the President enjoys considerable discretion in foreign policy and international affairs.Tharoor said that even when it comes to military action, the President can proceed without seeking approval for an initial period of up to 60 days. However, Congress can exercise its financial powers to restrict expenditure, particularly in the case of an expensive military campaign."Those in India who are expecting this to have some impact on our relationship with the US, I think, are completely mistaken," he said.Commenting on the election outcome, Tharoor described it as an extraordinary setback for the ruling party, pointing out that midterm elections traditionally serve as a course correction for the party in power.He also highlighted the gains made by candidates from minority communities and people of Indian origin, including the election of a mayor of Indian origin in Los Angeles.Tharoor said the results reflected the vibrancy of American democracy but maintained that the outcome would not significantly alter Trump's ability to take decisions on international affairs.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Jamie Dimon said on CLARITY Act allowing yield-paying stablecoins that JP Morgan will fight it, if we lose, we lose; here's how Democrat win means end of ...
articles.summary: The cryptocurrency industry's efforts to secure a comprehensive US regulatory framework could face a major setback after Democrats won control of both
articles.body: The cryptocurrency industry's efforts to secure a comprehensive US regulatory framework could face a major setback after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the midterm elections, with analysts warning that the long-debated CLARITY Act may struggle to advance. The development comes months after JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon vowed to fight provisions that could allow yield-paying stablecoins, arguing that such products pose risks similar to those seen in shadow banking. According to a CoinDesk report, several industry observers believe the Democratic victory has significantly reduced the chances of the CLARITY Act passing in its current form. Mati Greenspan, founder of Quantum Economics, described the Democratic sweep as potentially "the final nail in the CLARITY Act's coffin," noting that the legislation failed to clear a procedural Senate vote even when Republicans controlled both chambers. He said the crypto sector may now have to restart negotiations under a new political landscape.Jamie Dimon’s warning on CLARITY ActIn a Fox Business interview reported by The Globe and Mail in July, Dimon sharpened his criticism of the Digital Asset Market Clarity (CLARITY) Act, saying he feared yield-paying stablecoins could cause a “shadow banking” crisis. “We’ll fight it. If we lose, we lose, and we’ll live,” he said. Dimon argues that such tokens are effectively unregulated deposit-like products. Without capital requirements, he says, they could destabilise markets in a way similar to shadow banking in the 2008 financial crisis. In May, Dimon criticised Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong in a Fox Business interview, according to Bloomberg, using crude language to dismiss him. He said banks “will not accept” the current version of the bill.The bank-crypto fightThe CLARITY Act, intended to set a federal framework for digital assets, passed the House last year. It stalled in the Senate over whether crypto firms can pay yield on stablecoins. A compromise reached in May would ban passive rewards earned simply by holding tokens, but allow activity-based rewards tied to transactions or platform use.Coinbase and other exchanges back yield-bearing stablecoins, arguing they expand consumer choice and innovation. Banks, led by Dimon and the American Bankers Association, want them banned outright to protect deposits and financial stability. A ban would hit Circle, issuer of the USDC stablecoin, which earns interest on the cash and Treasuries backing its tokens, and Coinbase, which shares in Circle’s reserve income and earns fees from stablecoin trading.Democratic sweepCoinDesk reported that the crypto industry’s hopes for a regulatory framework took another blow when Democrats won both chambers. “For crypto, the Democratic sweep may well be the final nail in the Clarity Act’s coffin,” said Mati Greenspan, founder of Quantum Economics. He noted the bill couldn’t even clear a procedural vote in September, when Republicans controlled both chambers, and that the industry may now have to start from scratch in a divided Washington.Stefan Muehlbauer, head of US government affairs at CertiK, said the bill is likely dead in its current form. Anton Golub said crypto political action groups spent about $170.5 million on the elections, with at least $125.5 million going to Republicans. Despite Republican control of Congress and a crypto-friendly President Donald Trump, the bill failed to advance in September. Golub said Trump made regulators friendlier to the industry, but his family’s crypto involvement also gave Democrats a reason to oppose crypto-friendly legislation.Greater scrutiny expected for crypto sectorSeveral industry participants expect Democrats to take a more aggressive approach toward crypto oversight. CoinDesk reported that lawmakers could focus on issues including anti-money laundering controls, cybersecurity practices and consumer protection measures.Muehlbauer said congressional hearings and investigations may examine both cryptocurrency companies and President Trump's crypto-related business interests. Meanwhile, Shady El Damaty, co-founder of Human.tech, predicted increased scrutiny of tokenised stock offerings and broader crypto expansion efforts by trading platforms.Not everyone believes the legislation is beyond saving. Brent Fulfer, co-founder of venture capital firm TBV, noted that more than 70 House Democrats previously supported the CLARITY Act and argued that a revised bill with stronger safeguards and bipartisan backing could still gain traction.Crypto products expected to keep expandingWhile the regulatory outlook has become more uncertain, some industry executives believe innovation in digital asset products will continue. Golub said products such as perpetual futures are likely to grow beyond cryptocurrencies and expand into equities and other traditional financial markets.Jason Fernandes, founder of AdLunam, said the crypto industry should engage constructively with Democratic lawmakers rather than oppose stricter oversight outright. According to Fernandes, carefully targeted regulation and enforcement against bad actors could ultimately strengthen the broader crypto ecosystem.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: NCP's Praful Patel visits Sharad Pawar in hospital amid reported discontent with Sunetra
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: NCP leader Praful Patel on Thursday visited Nationalist Congress Party (SP) chief Sharad Pawar at Mumbai’s Breach Candy Hospital and enquired
articles.body: NEW DELHI: NCP leader Praful Patel on Thursday visited Nationalist Congress Party (SP) chief Sharad Pawar at Mumbai’s Breach Candy Hospital and enquired about his health. Patel said the veteran politician was stable and expected to return home in a day or two after completing his medical check-ups.The visit by Patel has triggered political speculation as he is among the NCP leaders reportedly "unhappy" with party boss Sunetra Pawar’s leadership. The meeting comes amid signs of internal discord within the party, adding a political dimension to Patel’s hospital visit.Sharad Pawar was admitted to Breach Candy Hospital on Wednesday night with a respiratory and chest infection, after being discharged from Pune’s Ruby Hall Clinic. Dr Pratit Samdani, a doctor at the hospital, said on Thursday that Pawar was stable and undergoing treatment."Sharad Pawar was admitted yesterday at Breach Candy Hospital for a respiratory and chest infection. He is stable and under treatment. He was admitted last night; he had a cough and an infection, something like bronchitis trouble. His treatment is ongoing, and he is currently stable," Dr Samdani told reporters.After meeting Pawar, Patel said the hospital admission was part of his routine medical check-ups and that his health was good. He also dismissed speculation that their meeting involved political discussions, saying he continued to meet Pawar and his daughter, Supriya Sule, because of their family ties.Also read: Rest, Supriya and I’ll look after country, PM Narendra Modi said to have told Sharad PawarIn a post on X, Patel said, "I visited the Breach Candy Hospital in Mumbai to pay a courtesy call on the esteemed Shri Sharad Pawar Saheb and inquired about his health."Providing an update on Pawar's condition, Patel said, "Sharad Pawar due to fatigue two days ago, was taken to Ruby Hall Clinic in Pune for a checkup. After that, he came to Mumbai, and here his health is fine. Naturally, a checkup happens once or twice a year, for a complete checkup, so in that context only he is admitted here at Breach Candy. His health is good. I am also happy that I came here, but everything is fine, and sahab was also in good spirits. He was asking about what is happening in politics in the country and state, as that is his interest. We had a good conversation, and I am happy that in a day or two all his checkups will be completed, so he will return home soon so he can rest."Patel also commented on Prime Minister Narendra Modi's conversation with Pawar, describing their relationship as long-standing and cordial. He said Modi's call to enquire about Pawar's health was natural given their association over the years.“Sharad Pawar and Narendra Modi have had a very long-standing relationship. I have also known Modi ji for many years and personally know about the relationship between him and Pawar sahab... I have witnessed their very good, cordial and respectful relationship over the years, even when we were in the UPA government in Delhi, and Modi ji was the Chief Minister of Gujarat... Modi ji is such a senior leader of the country today. So, if he received information about Sharad Pawar ji's health, it was natural for him to enquire about his well-being and speak to him...”Earlier, Pawar was admitted to Ruby Hall Clinic on November 2 after complaining of a cough and pleuritic chest pain. According to a statement issued by Dr Purvez K Grant, Chief Cardiologist, Chairman and Managing Trustee of the hospital, Pawar was stable and doing well at the time of his discharge."Mr Sharad Pawar has been discharged from Ruby Hall Clinic today. He is stable and doing well. He will be travelling directly from the hospital to his residence in Mumbai. We wish him good health and a speedy recovery," the statement said.His daughter, Baramati MP and NCP (SP) working president Supriya Sule, had earlier said that Pawar was undergoing medical tests and that his health parameters were stable. Ruby Hall Clinic subsequently said he would remain under observation as a precautionary measure. Doctors cleared him for discharge after his condition remained stable and his discomfort subsided.The developments come amid growing concerns within the BJP over organisational differences in its ally -- NCP. Union home minister Amit Shah met several senior NCP functionaries late Sunday who are believed to be unhappy with party president Sunetra Pawar and her son Parth, and urged them to resolve their differences in the party’s interest.Those who met Shah included NCP national working president Praful Patel, Maharashtra unit chief Sunil Tatkare, ministers Chhagan Bhujbal and Hasan Mushrif, and leaders Dhananjay Munde and Dilip Patil. Deputy chief minister Sunetra Pawar and her son Parth were absent from the meeting.Following the meeting, Sunetra Pawar convened a core committee meeting in Mumbai.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Israeli settlers seize 8 Palestinian homes in Jericho, displacing dozens
articles.summary: UN says settlers reportedly used live ammunition and beat Palestinians, forcing families to flee for their safety.
articles.body:
The United Nations has condemned the seizure of eight Palestinian homes by Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank city of Jericho, saying the settlers assaulted residents and forced dozens of people to flee.

Stephane Dujarric, a spokesperson for the UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, told reporters on Thursday that the settlers reportedly “used live ammunition” during the takeover on the previous day.

They also “physically assaulted Palestinian residents” and threw stones, “prompting the flight of families for their safety”, he said.

Some of those displaced now “lack adequate shelter”, while the Israeli military has since declared the area a closed military zone, preventing humanitarian workers from reaching those affected.

“We once again condemn all of these violent activities by the Israeli settlers,” he said.

The incident involved some 30 Israeli settlers, who came to take over the houses in Ein a-Duyuk a-Tahta on the outskirts of Jericho on Wednesday afternoon, according to Israeli settlement watchdog Peace Now.

The group said that, according to reports, the settlers “assaulted and robbed two Israeli activists and shot a Palestinian man in the leg” during the seizure.

The settlers claimed they legally purchased the homes, but Palestinian officials say the sale documents were forged.

Hanan Greenwood, a settler representative, told the AFP news agency that Nachala, a right-wing Israeli organisation, had bought the eight homes “with our help”. He said he was “very excited” to be there.

Nachala funds the establishment of new settlements in the occupied West Bank and campaigns for Israel to annex the territory.

But Hussein Hamayel, governor of the Jericho region, told the AFP that the land belongs to the Palestinian Authority and cannot be sold.

“What is being promoted is a forgery, not a sale, and what is being circulated is settler propaganda,” Hamayel said.

The land is located in the West Bank’s Area C, which has been under Israeli control since the Oslo Accords of the 1990s. Israel has occupied the West Bank since 1967, and more than 500,000 Israelis live in settlements there, which are illegal under international law.

Settler pogroms in the occupied West Bank have approached all-time highs this year, and several Palestinian communities in the greater Jericho area have already been driven from their homes.

Residents said they feared the new settlers would step up pogroms in the area and bring a heavier military presence.

That pattern has played out in Hebron, where some 400 settlers live in the Old City, in a city of about 250,000 Palestinians.

According to Peace Now, the Israeli presence in Hebron has notably “led to constant friction and violence, severe restrictions on Palestinian freedom of movement” and also “resulted in the displacement of thousands of Palestinians “.

articles.title: 3 criminals killed in encounter in Patna, SHO injured; weapons recovered
articles.summary: PATNA: At least three alleged criminals were killed in an encounter with police near the Ganga river in Sherpur, under the Maner police station area of
articles.body: PATNA: At least three alleged criminals were killed in an encounter with police near the Ganga river in Sherpur, under the Maner police station area of Bihar's Patna district, early Friday.Maner Station House Officer (SHO) Rajnish Kumar sustained a bullet injury to his left hand during the exchange of fire.The encounter took place during a joint operation conducted by the Patna Special Task Force (STF) and Patna Police. The three injured suspects were taken to hospital, where they were declared dead. The injured SHO was shifted to Patna for treatment.Patna Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Kartik Kumar Sharma said police teams were carrying out crime prevention operations when they received information that some criminals were allegedly planning a major incident in Sherpur.According to news agency ANI, Sharma said, “Police were preparing for operations as part of crime prevention. During this, the STF and the district police force were conducting operations in different areas. We received information that some criminals, who had a previous criminal history, had arrived here and were planning to carry out a major incident in Sherpur.”He said the suspects opened fire when the police team reached the location, and the SHO was injured in the retaliation.“When the police team reached this place, the criminals started firing. They were firing rapidly. During this, the Maner SHO and his team got out of their vehicle and retaliated. A bullet grazed the Maner SHO and passed through his uniform. The criminals also fired at other personnel,” he said.According to Sharma, three suspects were found injured after the firing stopped. They were rushed to a hospital, where doctors declared them dead.“When the police retaliated, some people were injured. articles.title: On Christmas Day 1945, American serviceman Frank Hayostek tossed a note in a bottle from his troopship; an Irish woman found it eight months later, and they exchanged letters for years
articles.summary: In 1945, American soldier Frank Hayostek sent a message in a bottle from his troopship, which was discovered by Irish woman Breda O'Sullivan. Their heartfelt exchange of letters spanned years, showcasing a unique bond forged across the Atlantic. Despite challenges, their story remains a remarkable symbol of connection and nostalgia.
articles.body: On Christmas night, 1945, 21-year-old American soldier Frank Hayostek found himself stuck on a troopship in the Atlantic, far away from home. He wrote a note, put it in an aspirin bottle and tossed it out into the sea, according to Message in a Bottle Hunter. Eight months later, it was found by a young Irish woman, Breda O’Sullivan, on a beach in County Kerry. That little gesture ignited a friendship that lasted for years.A lonely Christmas at sea War was over, and America wanted her soldiers back home for Christmas. The blog says President Truman intended to bring the 3 million service members back from overseas by then. There were a lot of people, and weather conditions only made everything even more difficult. Frank’s Liberty ship was caught in the storm, so he spent Christmas at sea, his third away from home. In his message, he mentioned that he had taken the idea from one of his boyhood fairy tales. He had no reward to offer the finder except for friendship, and asked for a reply.A dog, a beach, and a replyOn Friday 23 August 1946, Breda took the cows to a field by the sea and went for a walk. Her dog ran ahead, and she found a brown bottle with a piece of paper inside it. The cork crumbled apart in her fingers, but the note was dry. Breda said she thought at first that she was dreaming. The next day she replied, writing to Frank that she didn't want any reward; the surprise was enough. According to ABC News, they then swapped letters across the Atlantic for years. Frank kept every letter Breda wrote to him, but most of his letters to her are lost. Six years after the find, the plan was to meet in August 1952.When the press took overTrouble began after a simple interview. Frank appeared in an interview with a local paper in his hometown of Johnstown, Pennsylvania, in May 1952, talking about the bottle. The story passed quietly enough. Then, however, at the end of July, the story resurfaced and spread around the world. Even Time Magazine had a feature on it. Reporters tried to get hold of Breda before Frank did, in an attempt to spark a romance, but she wasn't interested in being photographed and got annoyed. Frank made it to Ireland on 5 August 1952, and stayed there for two weeks as reporters followed him around. Meanwhile, Breda had her cows to milk and her farm to work, leaving little time alone. According to the Courier Mail, as cited by the blog, when Frank got home, he tossed another aspirin bottle into the ocean.A friendship that faded A letter from Frank, found years later in his scrapbook, shows that he told Breda, during his visit, that he had once been married and that the marriage was annulled. Breda was a staunch Catholic, and she was hurt that he hadn't told her sooner. ABC News says the couple's romance never got off the ground. They wrote to each other for years, but the early warmth cooled, and the blog says the letter stopped in 1959. Frank married and had a son. He told The Kerryman in 2004 that he still thought about Breda every day. He died on 15 November 2009. His gravestone records his meeting with Breda, who found the bottle he had tossed from a Liberty ship.Why the story still resonates today Frank's note joined an old tradition. The US National Ocean Service says messages have been thrown into the sea for thousands of years for reasons of romance, distress, and science. It also points out that dumping anything into the ocean now violates US and international law. Frank and Breda never got together, and their story carries real sadness. Yet one note to the sea brought to strangers years of letters and a story that is still told today.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Anna Bissell took over her family’s carpet-sweeper business in 1889 after her husband’s death, becoming America’s first female CEO and leading the company for 42 years
articles.summary: Anna Bissell took charge of the family business in 1889 and became the first female chief executive in the United States.
articles.body: Anna Bissell took charge of the family business in 1889 and became the first female chief executive in the United States. The business had begun several years earlier, when Anna and Melville R. Bissell ran a crockery shop in Grand Rapids, Michigan. A problem with sawdust in the shop led Melville to invent an improved carpet sweeper, giving the couple a new product to sell. Anna was closely involved in the company from its early days, helping run its operations and market its sweepers.According to BISSELL, she led the company for 42 years, overseeing its growth into an international household name. Its account traces the business from a small shop to a major carpet-sweeper manufacturer.Anna Bissell's role in building the business before becoming its CEOMelville and Anna Bissell ran a small crockery shop in Grand Rapids, Michigan, in 1876. Sawdust was a constant problem in the shop, prompting Melville to invent an improved carpet sweeper. The product gave the couple a new business opportunity. They travelled to Philadelphia to sell the sweepers to distributors, dividing the work between them on State Street.Anna eventually outsold Melville, selling five or six dozen sweepers to Wanamaker’s, a high-fashion department store. In 1883, production moved from a makeshift shop to a five-story factory on Mill Street. The factory was struck by fire in 1884, but staff cleared the debris and resumed shipping products just 19 days later.Anna Bissell became America's first female CEO in 1889Anna was involved in the business from its earliest days, working in operations as well as marketing and sales. In 1889, she succeeded Melville and became America’s first female CEO. She remained at the helm for 42 years, from 1889 to 1931. During that period, BISSELL expanded and became an international household name.By the late 1880s and 1890s, the company had grown to 250 associates and said it held 75% of the world market. The company also reported that it had sold more than two million sweepers during its history, reflecting the product’s reach in homes and markets beyond the United States.BISSELL carpet sweepers reached international markets under Anna's leadershipThe carpet sweeper gained recognition beyond the United States during Anna’s leadership. In 1890, the BISSELL sweeper crossed the Atlantic, and Queen Victoria insisted that her palace be ‘Bisselled’ every week. The product later received awards at major international exhibitions. The Grand Rapids Sweeper won a gold medal at the Paris Exposition in 1900. Four years later, the BISSELL Sweeper received the Grand Prize at the World’s Fair in St. Louis. These milestones formed part of the company’s expansion during the period after Anna took charge. The business continued to build its reputation around the carpet sweeper, the invention that had emerged from the sawdust problem.Melville Bissell Jr. took over after Anna's 42-year leadershipAnna’s 42-year tenure ended in 1931, when Melville Bissell Jr. became president and took the company into the middle of the 20th century. The business continued to develop products for household cleaning in the decades that followed. In 1956, it introduced the ShampooMaster carpet shampooer, which the company said made scrubbing carpets on hands and knees a thing of the past.It launched its first electric product and combination vacuum and floor scrubbers in 1960. BISSELL later expanded into deep-cleaning machines, upright vacuums and products designed for homes with pets. articles.title: Australian woman shot during Bondi Beach attack dies almost a year later
articles.summary: The 90-year-old was among those seriously injured after gunmen opened fire at a Jewish event last year.
articles.body:
A 90-year-old woman who was shot during Australia's Bondi Beach attack last December has died in a Sydney hospital, almost a year after the mass fatal shootings.

Eva Geller was one of dozens who were seriously injured after two gunmen opened fire on a Jewish event in Bondi Beach on 14 December. Fifteen people were killed including a ten-year-old girl.

Rabbi Aron Moss from the Nefesh Synagogue said Geller, who escaped the Holocaust as a child, had remained as "positive, loving, and strong throughout her life, right until the end".

Australian leader Anthony Albanese has expressed his condolences, saying the country would never forget those who "continue to carry the pain" of last year's attacks.

The attack last December was Australia's worst mass shooting in almost three decades and prompted sweeping gun law reforms and a crackdown on hate speech.

One of the gunmen, Sajid Akram, 50, was killed by police at the scene. His son Naveed Akram was arrested and charged with 15 counts of murder , 40 charges of attempted murder and one count of committing a terrorist act. He remains before the courts.

Police have not provided any detail on possible further charges as a result of Geller's death.

On Friday, Rabbi Moss confirmed that Geller - who celebrated her 90th birthday earlier this year - had passed away last on Thursday night.

"She escaped the Holocaust as a child, eventually coming to Australia, and built a beautiful family," he said.

Her injuries from the shootings meant regular hospital treatment.

"Ever since being shot at the Bondi attack she'd been in and out of hospital, always wanting to come home. She was told she will never walk again but miraculously and with incredible determination she did walk again," said Rabbi Moss.

Geller had "came to shul (Yiddish for synagogue) this past High Holidays with an incredible show of strength," he added.

New South Wales police said it was aware the woman had died overnight and "are now awaiting further advice and are working with the office of the Coroner".

articles.title: 1 officer killed, 3 injured as gunman opens fire on police in Colorado
articles.summary: One officer was killed and three others wounded in a firefight with a suspect in Lakewood, a suburb of Denver, Colorado, on Thursday evening.
articles.body: One officer was killed and three others wounded in a firefight with a suspect in Lakewood, a suburb of Denver, Colorado, on Thursday evening. The shootout took place after police responded to a report of a suspicious person attempting to board a public bus. The suspect was also fatally shot by police during the exchange of gunfire.The shooting took place around 6.30pm when Lakewood police officers reached the bus following a call about the suspicious person, police spokesperson John Romero said during a news conference. The man opened fire as officers arrived. It was not immediately clear whether the shooting took place inside the bus or nearby.The three wounded officers were taken to hospital for treatment. Their conditions have not been disclosed. Another person was also injured in the incident, although the circumstances surrounding their injury remain unclear, Romero said.Police said the suspect may have been involved in a hit-and-run incident earlier in the day. However, authorities have not released his identity or provided further details about the possible connection.Lakewood Police are investigating the shooting and have urged the public to stay away from the area. The identities of the deceased officer, the injured officers and the suspect have not yet been made public.The Regional Transportation District (RTD), which operates public transport services in the area, said it was deeply concerned about the shooting.“RTD personnel responded to the incident immediately and are fully cooperating with the Lakewood Police Department as it conducts its investigation,” the statement said.You use AI every day. articles.title: Customers in Sussex are struggling to pay to fill their oil tanks
articles.summary: People in Sussex say they are taking on extra work and not heating their homes due to oil prices.
articles.body:
A woman from East Sussex says she is having to take on extra work to pay for the soaring cost of her heating oil.

Sheila Williams, from Golden Cross, has taken on a waitress job for the winter to help her pay her bills.

She said her oil bill had doubled since the start of 2026 and the extra job was needed to help pay for it.

A government spokesperson said: "We have pledged £53m in support for vulnerable households on heating oil and removed the 4% tariff on home heating oil."

Williams, who has lived alone in a park home for seven years, said: "Words cannot express how upset I am about this."

Thousands of homes across Sussex are not connected to the gas mains and rely on oil.

A household wanting to fill a 1,000-litre tank could be facing a bill of more than £970 .

Nigel Wanstall, from Sheffield Park, said: "We've no heating at all because I can't afford to fill my oil tank.

"We use an open fire in the lounge and an electric blanket in bed."

Jon Reardon is director at Rye Oil, which supplies 15,000 residents in south-east England.

He said: "On average the oil price has doubled since the war started in the Middle East.

"There are a lot of our customers trying to hold off ordering oil for as long as possible.

The issue of rising heating oil prices was debated in Westminster on Wednesday.

Polly Billington, energy minister, said the government was working to regulate the industry.

She said: "We are reforming the heating oil sector, holding suppliers to account and giving consumers confidence that they will get a fair deal."

articles.title: Special send-off marks final Scillonian III voyage
articles.summary: The Scillonian III started carrying passengers in 1977 and is making its last voyage on Sunday.
articles.body:
A ferry which has taken more than 5.3 million passengers between Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly is being given a special send-off as it retires from service.

The Scillonian III started carrying passengers in 1977 and is making its last voyage on Sunday, 8 November, with a special service on board and a flotilla escorting the vessel.

During its final voyage the crew will seal a special time capsule, filled with contributions from people who have taken voyages on the ship, to mark its 10,800 journeys over the last 49 years. The time capsule's final resting point is yet to be revealed.

Donations include photographs, pieces of memorabilia, artwork and keepsakes.

The ship which can carry 486 passengers will depart from Penzance at 09:00 GMT on Sunday and arrive at St Mary's at 11:45.

As she leaves St Mary's for the final time at 14:00 other Isles of Scilly Steamship Group vessels, the harbour master's vessel and a number of island gig and community boats will give it a special send-off.

The Cape Cornwall Singers are due to serenade it when the vessel arrives in Penzance at 16:45.

During its last week surveyors from whale and dolphin charity ORCA completed their final wildlife survey aboard the vessel.

Over the past 17 years, ORCA volunteers have completed more than 200 surveys on board, recording over 17 different species, according to Isles of Scilly Travel.

The replacement vessel Scillonian IV, which can carry 600 passengers, has departed the shipyard in Vietnam where it was built to be delivered to the UK.

articles.title: Critically endangered pied tamarin twins born at Devon zoo
articles.summary: Shaldon Wildlife Trust says it is one of two European zoos to breed the species in 2026.
articles.body:
One of the UK's smallest accredited zoos is celebrating after "extra special" pied tamarin twins were born at the site.

Shaldon Wildlife Trust, in Devon, said the critically endangered twins were born on 29 September to mum Bobby and dad Pedra. Its director, Zak Showell, said it was a "challenge" to breed the species.

The trust said the animals were among the most endangered primates in South America. Bosses said the infants were "thriving" and had started to hitch rides on their parents' backs as they explored their habitat.

Showell said: "For a zoo of our size to achieve this and to be one of just two European zoos to manage it this year is an unbelievable proud moment for our small team."

"It has been an incredible year for births here at Shaldon, but these twins are extra special," he said.

"Pied tamarins are exceptionally delicate animals, and breeding them successfully is a challenge."

The trust said the primates required "stress-free environments and specialist care".

It said zoo keepers intentionally kept the news of the arrivals under wraps for a few weeks to give the "delicate family complete peace and quiet".

The species is listed as critically endangered on the International Union of Conservation and Nature's (IUCN) Red List.

The zoo said, in the wild, they were restricted to "a shrinking pocket of rainforest" around Manaus, Brazil.

articles.title: Peterborough competition to turn aluminium cans into art
articles.summary: The contest aims to raise awareness of recycling old cans and is open to schools and groups.
articles.body:
Schools and community groups are being encouraged to collect old aluminium cans and turn them into pieces of art.

Peterborough City Council has come up with the idea of the Every Can Counts competition to encourage recycling of the cans and raise awareness of its importance to the environment.

The authority said the UK used about 10 billion cans a year, which is equivalent to 600 per household, but the recycling process used just 5% of the energy needed to create new aluminium.

The competition closes in May and entrants have been asked to create something that is 3D, free-standing, easily transportable and centred on the theme of Our Earth, Our Planet.

Cans can be glued together, painted and decorated, the authority added.

The three winners of the categories for primary and secondary schools and community groups will each receive gardening vouchers to spend on their school grounds or site.

Their artwork will also go on display at the Peterborough Celebrates Festival at Ferry Meadows in June.

Chris Wiggin, the council's Liberal Democrat cabinet member for the environment, said: "I would urge school pupils and members of community groups to take part in Every Can Counts and help us spread the word about the importance of recycling.

"As a council we are fully committed to increasing recycling rates across Peterborough and encouraging everyone to play their part in this. I'm looking forward to seeing the entries and would like to wish everyone the very best of luck."
